title: Countable types in ultraproducts

based_on.title: Ultrafilters Throughout Mathematics
based_on.pages: 92–93 (§6.6, Definition 6.6.3, Exercise 6.6.7 and Lemma 6.6.9); 127–128 (§8.2, Theorem 8.2.1 and Remark 8.2.2)

summary: Realize countable finitely satisfiable types in countably incomplete ultraproducts by choosing finite coordinate witnesses, and deduce aleph-one saturation in countable languages.
abstract: A nonstandard natural number can exceed every ordinary natural number even though each coordinate of a representing sequence is finite. The same idea can solve much more general countable lists of first-order conditions. We show that an ultraproduct realizes every such list whose finite parts already have solutions, provided its ultrafilter admits a decreasing sequence of large sets with empty intersection. Each coordinate is assigned only finitely many conditions, but every fixed condition is assigned on a large set; the resulting sequence gives one solution to them all. Parameters retain their original values throughout. For a countable language, this realizes all types over countable parameter sets and gives aleph-one saturation, a stronger property than saturation over finite parameter sets. The resulting structure need not have countable size.
